quarterly_data.signal: Positive high-level results from a planned interim analysis of the DeLLphi-305 Phase III trial: Imfinzi (durvalumab) plus Amgen's Imdelltra (tarlatamab) showed a statistically significant and highly clinically meaningful improvement in overall survival (primary endpoint) versus Imfinzi alone as 1st-line maintenance treatment of extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC) in patients who had not progressed after Imfinzi plus platinum-etoposide induction, and also statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements in the secondary endpoints of progression-free survival and objective response rate. The trial is sponsored by Amgen, with partial funding and Imfinzi provided by AstraZeneca; 563 patients were randomised 1:1, safety was consistent with the individual treatments with no new safety signals, and the data will be presented at a forthcoming medical meeting and shared with global regulatory authorities. The company estimates 195,000 people globally will be treated for ES-SCLC in 2026, with median OS on the current standard of care of approximately one year. Imfinzi is approved in the US, EU, Japan, China and many other countries as standard of care in ES-SCLC (CASPIAN) and limited-stage SCLC (ADRIATIC); the company calls it the first and only immunotherapy combined with a bispecific T-cell engager to show a survival benefit in this setting (company claim).
quarterly_data.figure: DeLLphi-305 OS primary endpoint met, PFS and ORR also significant (high-level results, no numbers released); 563 patients; an estimated 195,000 people treated for ES-SCLC globally in 2026
